en.t: If AI finishes a draft in two minutes, how long does it take to make it usable?
en.d: I'd count the checking, rewriting, formatting, and correcting too. That's the time the person doing the work actually feels. It makes the comparison more honest: how long did the task take before, and how long does it take now, with a result you'd accept? Where does most of your AI review time go? #AI #Productivity #Automation #ProcessImprovement…

en.t: Teaching data analysis to Operations colleagues made me question things I did on autopilot.
en.d: Explaining a technical process to someone who needs to make a business decision takes care. You have to understand what they actually need from it. I bring that same question to AI: can the person receiving this answer use it to decide what happens next? That's a useful test for a dashboard, a chatbot, or a two-paragraph explanation. #AI #DataAnalytics…

en.t: Before automating a task, try explaining how you do it to someone new.
en.d: Notice where you say, "It depends," "I usually just know," or "Ask me when that happens." Those are the parts I'd want to understand before handing the task to AI. They often contain the judgment that keeps the process working. Writing down the exceptions can be useful work on its own. Which part of your job is hardest to explain? #AI #Automation…

en.t: Explaining the same project to AI in every new conversation sounds exhausting.
en.d: I'd rather keep a short project note: the goal, the audience, the terms we use, and the decisions already made. Then update it when something changes. It also gives me something concrete to review when an answer goes off track. Did the AI miss the context, or did I give it an outdated version? What belongs in your project note? #AI #KnowledgeManagement…

en.t: A confident AI answer makes me want to check the source.
en.d: If it says sales grew 12%, I want to see the dates, the calculation, and the data behind it. Were returns included? Are we comparing the same stores? Those details change what the number means and what someone might do with it. For AI-assisted analysis, being able to trace an answer matters to me as much as how clearly it's written. #AI #DataAnalytics…

en.t: Imagine a meeting summary that says, "The team agreed to launch."
en.d: In the meeting, one person supported it, two raised concerns, and nobody made a final decision. That's why I'd ask an AI summary to separate decisions, open questions, and disagreements. A smooth paragraph can hide exactly what the next meeting needs to resolve. When you review a summary, check what happened to the uncertainty. What do you usually find…
